mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and economic support.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks materialize.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeded 7.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which depresses corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced profit margins.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, as measured by Rank IC below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contractions (INDPRO < 95.0), manufacturing output declines signal weakening real economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recessionary fears dominate market sentiment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO fell below 95.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over the prior month indicates persistent inflation that erodes corporate profit margins and prompts monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as valuation multiples compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rose over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 230.0, it signals an inflation acceleration that triggers immediate Federal Reserve policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets price in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeded 230.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved economic outlook.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, as measured by Rank IC below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), higher interest rates suppress economic activity and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise and growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeded 2.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
